# Kepler

> Kepler is GitKraken's Agentic Development Environment (ADE). It pulls every issue and pull request assigned to you into one place, then hands any of it to the coding agent you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Auggie, OpenCode, Grok Build, Pi, or Google Antigravity) with the context already attached.

Scope: 29 pages included. Excluded (3): environment-and-setup.md, kepler-New-Page-Template.md, workflow-views.md.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started with Kepler](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-getting-started/): Install Kepler on Windows, macOS, or Linux, connect an agent and your trackers, and put an agent on real work in a few minutes.
- [Quick Answers](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/quick-answers/): Short answers to common Kepler questions, each linked to the full page. Run agents on Windows, in WSL, or on another machine, use several accounts of one agent, check on agents from your phone, set up every new worktree automatically, and have a second agent review the work.

## Core Concepts

- [The Kepler Interface](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-interface/): Kepler opens on your work - every issue and pull request assigned to you, alongside the tasks you already have running. Learn how to read it, work several items side by side, and start work from it.
- [Arranging Your Work](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/arranging-your-work/): One interface means you shape it rather than switch away from it. Choose an arrangement, group, sort and filter the list, save a combination as a named view, set a task's progress, and archive in bulk.
- [Actions](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/actions/): Actions are editable named prompts you fire at a task, issue, or pull request. Learn the four built-in Actions, how to change them, how to write your own, and how to have a different agent review the code than the one that wrote it.
- [Tasks and Resources](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/tasks-and-resources/): A Task is the unit of work in Kepler. Learn what a Task holds, how worktrees work, and how everything attached to a Task reaches your agents.
- [The Task View](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/task-view/): Open a Task to see its resources, agent sessions, changes, and files side by side. Learn the header, the rail, columns and free-form tabs, the file viewer, and how to start sessions from a draft tab and open terminals.
- [The Agent Graph](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-graph/): A live graph of everything your agents are doing - every task, session, turn, tool call, subagent, and file, drawn as it happens.

## Working in Kepler

- [Create a Task](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/create-task/): Start a Task from an issue, a pull request, or nothing at all, with the repository, branch, and context already attached.
- [Agent Sessions](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-sessions/): An agent session is one running conversation with a coding agent inside a Task. Learn how to start one, pick the agent and account (including several accounts of the same agent), queue prompts, answer the agent's questions and permission requests, track usage limits, and keep sessions running through restarts.
- [Ask Kepler](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/ask-kepler/): Ask Kepler is a chat and a terminal in a panel beside whatever you're looking at. Ask what needs you, have it check on your tasks and sessions, hand a chat on to a new task, or open a quick shell that belongs to no task.
- [Review Changes](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/review-changes/): An agent finished. Read the diff in the Changes overlay, comment on it, stage and commit, update the branch from its base, resolve update conflicts with AI, and hand the rest to AI Sync or AI Compose.
- [Voice Input](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/voice-input/): Dictate to an agent instead of typing. Voice input transcribes on your device with Qwen3-ASR, or with Whisper where WebGPU is unavailable, learns the words you fix, works push-to-talk or hands-free, and is available in remote windows.

## Integrations

- [Agent Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-integrations/): Kepler runs the coding agent you already have. Connect Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Auggie, OpenCode, Grok Build, Pi, or Google Antigravity, or add your own custom agent.
- [MCP Servers](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/mcp-servers/): See the MCP servers each agent loads, turn a server or a single tool on or off per repository or for every repository, add and remove servers, and sign in to the ones that need it, from inside Kepler.
- [Issue Tracker Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations/): Connect your issue trackers to Kepler, cloud or self-hosted, so the issues you're working on land in one list, with everything an agent needs already attached.
- [Pull Request Integrations](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/pull-request-integrations/): Connect your Git hosts to Kepler, cloud or self-hosted, so the pull requests you authored and the ones waiting on your review land in one list, already matched to the worktrees they belong to.

## Configuration

- [Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings/): An overview of Kepler's Settings, covering the 15 Settings pages and where each is documented, finding a setting, sub-pages and unsaved changes, settings in a remote window, and deep links with section anchors.
- [Setup and Account Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-setup-account/): The Setup and Account entries at the top of Kepler's Settings, covering the first-run setup checklist, who you're signed in as, your organization and plan, what your plan unlocks, GitKraken AI credits and usage by feature, and trials.
- [Agent Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-agents/): The Agents page of Kepler's Settings, covering your agents and their accounts, default session mode, artifacts, custom agents, MCP servers, agent tools, approvals, and usage limits.
- [Task Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-tasks/): The Tasks page of Kepler's Settings, covering the default agent, what new sessions start with, where new tasks make changes, branch prefix, folder locations and the Variables menu, task naming, and the task page.
- [Repository Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-repositories/): The Repositories page of Kepler's Settings, covering the repositories folder, adding and editing repositories, per-repository branch prefixes and commands, cleaning up and updating worktrees and branches, and Projects.
- [Integration Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-integrations/): The Integrations page of Kepler's Settings, covering issue tracker and Git host connections, and sessions started in your own terminal.
- [Action Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-actions/): The Actions page of Kepler's Settings, covering preferred Actions per kind of item and the Action list, with a link to the full Actions guide.
- [App Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-app/): The app pages of Kepler's Settings, covering General (language, windows, default editor, keeping agents running), Notifications, Appearance (themes, chat, terminal, code, diff view), Voice input, and Keyboard shortcuts.
- [Environment Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-environment/): The Remote environments and Remote Access pages of Kepler's Settings, covering the machines your agents can run on over SSH or WSL, remote windows, and opening this Kepler from another device.
- [Update and Help Settings](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-updates-help/): The Updates and Help pages of Kepler's Settings, covering the installed version and app updates, the docs, release notes, onboarding guides, and Kepler's logs.
- [Remote Environments](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/remote-environments/): Run your agents on another machine over SSH or in WSL, switch environments from the title bar, manage machines in Settings, forward an SSH host's ports to this computer, and open this Kepler from another device, including your phone, with Remote Access.

## Release Notes

- [Kepler 0.x](https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/release-notes-current/): View the latest features, improvements, and fixes shipping in the current version of Kepler.
